subject.title: Feature/Fix: Add conservative lineage safety and promotion controls

question: Should CodexBar adopt this four-PR lineage engine as the canonical solution for https://github.com/steipete/CodexBar/issues/2037, or prefer the narrower scanner repair in https://github.com/steipete/CodexBar/pull/2118?
rationale: Both approaches target fork-accounting errors, but they differ substantially in scope, operational complexity, cache model, rollout path, and long-term maintenance cost; repository policy requires explicit sign-off for that architectural choice.

options.title: Keep lineage shadow-only pending proof
options.body: Review the stack sequentially and retain legacy authority until exact-head real-corpus evidence proves the complete promotion and rollback path.

options.title: Prefer the narrow repair
options.body: Land the focused identity and cache-invalidation changes from https://github.com/steipete/CodexBar/pull/2118 and defer the broader lineage architecture unless residual failures remain.

options.title: Adopt the lineage stack
options.body: Choose the four-PR architecture as the permanent direction after its dependencies, performance evidence, and upgrade behavior receive explicit approval.

recommendation.title: Keep lineage shadow-only pending proof
recommendation.body: Review the stack sequentially and retain legacy authority until exact-head real-corpus evidence proves the complete promotion and rollback path.

likelyOwner.reason: The repository owner has recent history in the affected cost-scanner code and is the strongest available owner for the architecture and rollout decision.
